articles.title: Accessibility tools
articles.body:
# Accessibility tools

The accessibility button in the title bar opens text size, high contrast, reduce motion, always-visible focus, larger targets, keyboard help and read-aloud.

You can hide the button. It asks first, with Cancel focused. Bring it back from Settings search, the command palette, or **Reset accessibility tools**.

articles.title: Appearance editor
articles.body:
# Appearance editor

Right-click any element, or press `Shift+F10` on it, and choose **Edit appearance…**. The panel styles that one element and shows the change live.

- **States:** style the element at rest, on hover, on keyboard focus, and while pressed. A dot marks states that have changes.
- **Properties:** font, size, weight, italic, underline, strikethrough, all capitals, letter spacing, text colour, background, border colour, corner radius, glow and opacity. Each property has its own Reset.
- **Undo and redo:** `Ctrl+Z` and `Ctrl+Y` (or `Ctrl+Shift+Z`) while the panel is open, up to 100 steps for this window.
- **Copy and paste style:** copy one element's style and paste it onto another.
- **Presets:** name a style and apply it to any element later.
- **Reset:** reset one property, one element, or every element (with the super confirmation). Presets stay.
- **Export and import:** styles save as UTF-8 JSON with the schema `aws-app-deployer.appearance/1`. Imported files are checked property by property; anything unknown or out of range is dropped and never reaches the page.

Styles live in your settings file under `appearance`, so they appear in local history and can be restored from there.

articles.title: Attention modes
articles.body:
# Attention modes

Five separate modes in **Settings > Focus and comfort**. Each one is off until you turn it on, and any mix works. They are interface options, not medical advice.

- **Focus:** dims everything except the row, card or setting you are on. Nothing is hidden; hover or move keyboard focus to bring anything forward.
- **Low stimulation:** quieter colour, no extra motion, and only notifications that need you pop up. Every message still lands in the notification list. Your system's reduced-motion setting is always respected as well.
- **Time awareness:** the title bar shows how long the app has been open and how long since you last changed something. Just the numbers.
- **One thing at a time:** write one next action; it stays at the top of every screen and survives a restart. **Done** clears it.
- **Momentum:** when a deployment draft has not changed for 30 minutes, a small note offers to reopen it. **Not now** hides it for one hour.

The landing page has the same five modes in its accessibility tools, adapted to a page: Focus dims other sections, Time awareness shows time on the page, and Momentum appears after 10 quiet minutes. School mode leaves all five available.

## Funny levels

English and Cantonese each have their own funny level from 1 (plain) to 5 (very playful). Both start at 5. The level styles every kind of message, errors and warnings included, while names, accounts, numbers and errors stay exact. School mode uses level 1.

articles.title: Changelog
articles.body:
# Changelog

Help opens the changelog: every released version with its date, its changes grouped as Added, Changed, Fixed or Removed, and each commit's SHA linking to GitHub. Filter by date and search with regex, then copy or export the filtered view.

articles.title: Deployment charts
articles.body:
# Deployment charts

The Deployments screen shows two charts built only from records on this computer:

- **Deployment time:** minutes for the last 12 deployments that recorded timing. Stopped deployments show as amber points. Hover a point for its name and time.
- **Outcomes:** healthy and stopped deployments for each of the last 7 days.

Records made before timing was added have no duration, and none is guessed. **Table view** shows the same numbers as plain tables for screen readers and copying. With reduced motion on, the line appears without drawing in.

articles.title: Command palette
articles.body:
# Command palette

Press `Ctrl+Shift+F` anywhere. Type to search every destination and command. Turn on **Regex** to use a regular expression; each token is explained as you type and invalid patterns are named. Arrow keys move, Enter runs, Escape closes.

articles.title: Context menus
articles.body:
# Context menus

Right-click any element, or press `Shift+F10`, for actions that fit it: open or copy a deployment link, select, export, remove, reset a setting, copy text. Every menu starts with a filter field and its own regex builder. Shortcuts shown in a menu are the ones that work.

articles.title: Deploying
articles.body:
# Deploying

Press **New deployment**.

1. Account: the verified account and region.
2. Source: choose a `Dockerfile` or a `compose.yaml`. The app inspects it and lists anything it cannot deploy yet before creating anything.
3. Configure: application name, container port, health check path and plain environment values. Task size is fixed at 0.25 vCPU and 512 MiB.
4. Review and **Deploy**.

Progress comes from the backend, stage by stage. The link appears only after AWS reports healthy targets and the link answers. If a release fails its health checks, ECS rolls back and the previous version keeps serving.

articles.title: Deployment records
articles.body:
# Deployment records

The Deployments screen lists the result recorded when each deployment finished on this computer. Open the filter to search by name, region or error, with or without regex, and by status. Select records to export them as JSON, YAML, CSV or Markdown, or remove them after a two-key confirmation. Removals stay in local history and can be restored.

articles.title: Dim sum surprise
articles.body:
# Dim sum surprise

Now and then, at launch, a dim sum dish appears in the corner with its English and Cantonese names and its photo from the public catalog. It never interrupts setup or a running deployment. Its switch in Settings cannot turn it off, and says so. School mode hides it.

articles.title: Export
articles.body:
# Export

Records, history and settings export as JSON, YAML, CSV or Markdown, or all together as a ZIP. Each export states its schema, UTF-8 encoding and LF line endings. CSV and Markdown write nested values as JSON text in one cell; the export says so before it runs.

articles.title: Getting started
articles.body:
# Getting started

Open the app. Setup checks this computer for AWS CLI v2.22 or later and Docker, and lists the AWS CLI profiles on your Windows account.

- If a tool is missing, press **Install missing tools**. See [one-click setup](one-click-setup).
- Pick a profile and press **Continue** to sign in. See [signing in](signing-in).
- Then start a deployment from the New deployment button. See [deploying](deploying).

Deployments create real AWS resources that cost money until you delete them in AWS.

articles.title: Keyboard
articles.body:
# Keyboard

- `Ctrl+Shift+F` command palette
- `Ctrl+N` new deployment
- `Ctrl+,` settings
- `F1` keyboard help
- `Shift+F10` or the menu key: context menu for the focused element
- `Alt+Arrows` move a focused panel, add `Shift` to resize
- `Esc` clears a filter, then closes

articles.title: Language and wording
articles.body:
# Language and wording

- **Language**: English, Hong Kong Cantonese, or both side by side.
- **Funny level**: 1 to 5 changes how playful the wording around a result is. Facts and safety warnings never change.
- **Personal wording**: drop a JSON file anywhere in the app, or choose one in Settings, shaped like `{"version": 1, "entries": {"Deploy": "Ship"}}`. It is checked as a whole and applied all at once or not at all. **Clear** restores the original words.

## Voices

With **Read status aloud** on, choose a separate installed voice for English and for Cantonese, and set pitch and speed. **Try this voice** plays a short sample. When no voice for a language is installed, the setting says so instead of guessing.

## Wording celebration

Dropping a valid wording file plays a short celebration with a tada sound. Reduced motion, calm mode and school mode show a quiet badge instead, and sounds follow the Action sounds setting.

articles.title: Local history
articles.body:
# Local history

Every settings change and record removal is kept, append-only, beside the app's data. Open Local history from New tab. Filter by category, search with regex, and pick a date range. Select a revision to see what changed. **Restore** adds a new revision; nothing is rewritten. Export the history as JSON, YAML, CSV, Markdown or a ZIP.

articles.title: Logo
articles.body:
# Logo

In **Settings > Logo**, pick a symbol, a shape (rounded, circle or square) and a background colour, or use your own PNG, JPEG or WebP image up to 256 KB. The file's contents are checked to be a real image on this computer; SVG and other formats are refused. The logo shows in the title bar. **Reset** returns to the standard icon.

articles.title: Notifications
articles.body:
# Notifications

Results appear as toasts at the bottom of the window. Errors stay until you dismiss them. The bell opens the notification centre: search with or without regex, select all shown, invert, copy or dismiss in bulk.

articles.title: One-click setup
articles.body:
# One-click setup

**Install missing tools** installs AWS CLI v2 and Docker Desktop without opening any download page.

## How it works
- It tries Windows Package Manager first, silently.
- If that is missing or fails, it downloads the publisher's installer from `awscli.amazonaws.com` or `desktop.docker.com`, checks the Authenticode signature, and deletes the file without running it if the signature is wrong.
- It installs silently, then refreshes PATH so the tools are found.

## Problems it fixes
- Interrupted downloads resume and retry up to 3 times.
- WSL not ready for Docker is enabled and updated.
- Docker installed but stopped is started, and the app waits for its engine.

Windows asks for your permission once. The app never answers that prompt. If you decline it, or a company policy blocks the installer, the app says exactly which.

articles.title: Scheduled settings
articles.body:
# Scheduled settings

In **Settings > Scheduled settings**, add rules such as "Theme to Dark, every day at 19:00" or "Low stimulation on, Monday to Friday at 22:00".

- Settings that can be scheduled: theme, language, accent colour, reduce motion, focus, low stimulation, time awareness, action sounds, emoji and the app name.
- For each setting, the rule whose time passed most recently wins, looking back up to a week. Rules are checked every 30 seconds.
- Changing a scheduled setting yourself holds until that setting's next rule.
- Settings show where their value came from: set by you, default, scheduled right now, or from the external source.

## External source

Turn on **Read settings from a URL** to check an http or https address every few minutes. It can return either a JSON object of settings, for example `{"settings": {"theme": "dark", "calm": "on"}}`, or a Home Assistant entity state such as `/api/states/input_select.theme`, which is mapped to the setting you choose. An optional access token is sent as a Bearer token and kept encrypted with Windows protected storage, never in settings, history or exports. Unknown settings and invalid values are ignored and listed. If a check fails, nothing changes and the reason is shown.

Scheduled rules win over the external source. School mode keeps the language in English whatever a rule says. The landing page has scheduled rules for its own settings in the accessibility panel.

articles.title: School mode
articles.body:
# School mode

School mode is one switch shared by every app from this publisher on your Windows user. Turn it on in **Settings > Focus and comfort** or from the command palette.

While it is on:

- Everything is shown in English.
- Funny levels, personal wording, the Cantonese and bilingual options, the dim sum surprise and release code names are removed from every screen, search result and notification.
- Your earlier choices stay saved and come back when you turn it off.

You can rename the mode. After a rename, the app uses only your chosen name.

Turning it on the first time asks you to set a PIN or password. Turning it off asks for it again. After 5 wrong tries the app waits before the next try, starting at 30 seconds and doubling up to an hour. Only a scrypt hash is stored, in `school-mode.json` inside the shared `Ding-Ding-Projects Shared` folder in your app data. This is a speed bump, not security: deleting that file resets it, and the panel tells you where the file is.

The landing page has the same mode in its accessibility panel. It is stored only in that browser, with a PBKDF2 hash of the PIN, and clearing the site's data resets it.

articles.title: Settings
articles.body:
# Settings

Every setting has an info button above its control. It explains what the setting does, says whether the value came from your settings file or the built-in default, and offers a practice run that never changes the real value.

Search settings from the top of the Settings screen. Right-click a setting for **Reset to default**.

## Colour picker

Press **Pick** next to the custom colour to open the colour picker: a saturation and brightness square (drag, or use the arrow keys), a hue slider and an opacity slider. It reads and writes hex with alpha, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()` and colour names, and shows the WCAG contrast ratio against the page background with a plain verdict.

## Funny level on every message

Every notification is styled by the funny level for its language, errors and warnings included. The facts in the message never change. School mode turns the styling off.

articles.title: Signing in to AWS
articles.body:
# Signing in to AWS

The app uses AWS CLI browser sign-in for IAM Identity Center.

- Choose a profile in Accounts and press **Sign in with browser**.
- Approve the request in your browser. The window comes back to the front by itself.
- The app checks who you are with AWS STS and shows the account ID, role, ARN, profile and region.

Tokens are never shown. Each Windows user keeps their own profiles. Signing in to AWS gives the app permission to deploy; it never adds a sign-in to your deployed site.

articles.title: Confirming destructive actions
articles.body:
# Confirming destructive actions

Removing records asks for two keys and a slide. Turn both keys by clicking them or pressing R and M, then slide all the way. **Emergency exit** or Escape cancels at any point, and nothing happens until both keys and the slide are complete.

articles.title: Tabs
articles.body:
# Tabs

The Workspace tab holds the main screens. Ordinary navigation never opens tabs. Press **New tab** to open a utility tab from the catalog: local history, docs, changelog, settings, help or accounts. Search the catalog with or without regex. Right-click a tab to close it or close the others.

articles.title: Tools: Base64 and file converter
articles.body:
# Tools: Base64 and file converter

Open **New tab** and choose **Tools**. Everything runs on this computer and nothing is uploaded.

## Base64 toolkit

Encode UTF-8 text, decode Base64 (standard or URL-safe), or turn any file up to 10 MB into Base64. Decoded data that is not UTF-8 text is reported as binary and can be saved as a file.

## File converter

Up to 25 MB per file: JSON to YAML or CSV, CSV to JSON or YAML, Markdown to HTML (scripts and unsafe links are removed), and images between PNG, JPEG and WebP. Converting a transparent image to JPEG fills the transparency with white. Rows for formats that need a tool this app does not include (YAML reading, video and audio, 7z and RAR) are shown disabled with the missing tool named.

## Open in an editor

Results can open in VS Code, when it is installed, or in the default app for that file type. The file is written to the `handoff` folder inside the app data folder first.

articles.title: Updates
articles.body:
# Updates

Installed copies check for updates at start and every 4 hours. When one is ready, a banner shows its version with **Restart to install update** and **Later**. Builds are unsigned, so Windows may show an unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warning. Help shows the current update state and has **Check for updates**.

articles.title: What a deployment creates
articles.body:
# What a deployment creates

- A VPC across two availability zones
- A public Application Load Balancer
- One NAT gateway for outbound traffic
- Two Fargate tasks in private subnets
- An ECR repository holding an immutable image
- CloudWatch logs

These are billed by AWS until you delete them. Closing the app never deletes infrastructure.
